clue.text: Words belie resolution to clean up texts

indicators.note: resolution is read as resolving or breaking down, so the letters of the two words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A dispute in which someone's words contradict their own determination to purge offensive writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' looks like a firm intention, but it signals that WORDS BELIE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To expurgate a book is to strip out the passages thought offensive, after Thomas Bowdler's censored Shakespeare.

clue.text: Ring ahead of time for medical application

parts.note: a band is a ring, as on a finger
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Phone before a set hour to make an appointment for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests a phone call, but it is a band.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of material wrapped around a wound is applied to dress it.

clue.text: Turn on second, grieved at having suffered blows

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as a handle
wept means cried in grief

explanation.surface: Someone turns on a second person, upset at having taken a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows' suggests punches, but means gusts of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A place exposed to strong gales has been battered by the wind.

clue.text: Financial backing for worthy landlord?

parts.note: a landlord lets property, so is one who lets
of credit means creditable, deserving praise

explanation.surface: Money support offered to a deserving publican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landlord' suggests a pub owner, but here means one who lets a property out.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank document guaranteeing payment on a buyer's behalf is a standard instrument of trade finance.

clue.text: Get money for new English serial

indicators.note: new means the letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Sell the rights to a fresh English television series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes the answer from E and SERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell an asset and turn it into cash is to convert it to money.

clue.text: Cut and run, securing match finally

indicators.note: securing means the word for run holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a single is one run in cricket

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word match

explanation.surface: Snip and dash off, after striking the last match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut and run' looks like an idiom, but 'Cut' is the definition. To shingle hair is to crop it short at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To shingle is to crop hair short at the back of the head in a tapering style.

clue.text: Principal boy embracing heroine at last

indicators.note: embracing means the word for boy holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word heroine

explanation.surface: A pantomime principal boy hugging the heroine in the closing scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes pantomime, where the 'principal boy' is a role; here 'Principal' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The main or chief role is the starring part, as in the lead actor.

clue.text: Gives out Times freely

indicators.note: freely means the letters of the word are loosened and rearranged at will

explanation.surface: The newspaper is distributed free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges the letters of TIMES; the surface plays on the newspaper the puzzle appears in.
explanation.definitionFit: To send out or discharge something, such as light or sound, is to release it.

clue.text: Presented performing in old hat

indicators.note: in means the word for performing goes inside the word for old-fashioned

parts.note: something old hat is out of date
an actor who is on is performing on stage

explanation.surface: Given an award while performing in an antique hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' looks like headgear, but means old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handed over as a gift has been given or bestowed.

clue.text: Nursery guardian whose spell finished at midnight

definitions.text: Nursery guardian whose spell finished at midnight

parts.words: Nursery guardian whose spell finished at midnight
parts.note: a protective magical figure from children's stories whose enchantment in the Cinderella tale wore off as the clock struck twelve

explanation.surface: A nanny whose shift ended at midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursery' means nursery tales and 'spell' means magic, not a nanny's period of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cinderella, a benevolent magical protector conjures a coach and gown that vanish at twelve.

clue.text: Musical group given half of score on returning

indicators.note: returning means the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: a score is twenty, so half of it is ten
taken as written

explanation.surface: A band is handed half a musical score when it comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' suggests sheet music, but it is the number twenty; TEN followed by ON gives TENON, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nine players or singers is a standard ensemble size in chamber music.

clue.text: Quick quality of film technique

definitions.meaning: quick in its old sense of alive: the quality of liveliness or vivacity
the making of cartoons by photographing a series of drawings frame by frame

explanation.surface: A remark on the brisk character of a cinematic method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' is meant in the sense of living or lively, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both spirited liveliness and the cartoon-making process of bringing drawings to life on screen.

clue.text: Main points summarised in a call, meeting the case

indicators.note: in means the compass letters sit inside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
to ring is to telephone, a call
the main points of the compass, north, south, west and east, shortened to their initials

explanation.surface: Key points are condensed into a phone call that deals with the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main points' looks like the gist of an argument, but means the cardinal points of the compass, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that satisfies or corresponds to requirements is said to fit the case.

clue.text: Son in row sent back for further examination

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for son goes inside the reversed row
sent back means the word for row is reversed

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A boy placed in a row of desks is made to sit a test again.
explanation.walkthrough: TIER reversed is REIT, and S goes inside it. In Britain, a RESIT is an exam taken again after failing.
explanation.definitionFit: A second attempt at a failed exam is a fresh test of the candidate.

clue.text: What makes it difficult to see it's an unpleasant prospect?

definitions.text: What makes it difficult to see
definitions.meaning: read literally, a sore eye, an ailment that hampers vision

explanation.surface: Someone asks what spoils the view and calls it a grim outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the answer literally as an eye that is sore.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ugly that spoils a view is a blot on the landscape.

clue.text: Intellectual output from battery commander

parts.note: battery hens are kept in cages to lay eggs, so their produce is an egg
a head is a leader or commander

explanation.surface: A clever soldier is the product of an artillery officer's unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battery' suggests artillery, but it is a battery farm for hens.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainy, bookish person is called this informally, often mockingly.

clue.text: Holding up negative left for development

indicators.note: development suggests reworking, so the letters are rearranged into new form

explanation.surface: A photographer keeps back a negative, leaving it to be developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for development' turns NEGATIVE plus L into the answer; the surface plays on developing film.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising something up, physically or morally, is lifting it.

clue.text: Small piece missing front page in paper

definitions.text: Small piece missing front page in paper

indicators.note: missing front means the first letter is dropped from the word for small piece

parts.note: a particle is a tiny piece

explanation.surface: A short item that fails to make the front page of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTICLE without its front P gives the answer, and the whole clue also describes a short news item tucked away inside the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of writing printed in a newspaper is the usual name for a news item.

clue.text: By all accounts, one should be satisfied

definitions.text: By all accounts, one should be satisfied

parts.words: By all accounts, one should be satisfied
parts.note: read literally: a person who must be satisfied by every set of financial accounts before signing them off

explanation.surface: Everyone says a person ought to be content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By all accounts' is an idiom for 'reportedly', but here means by every set of books examined.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector of company books must be content with the figures before approving them.

clue.text: Elaborate, no longer simple

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
plain means simple

explanation.surface: Something ornate that has ceased to be plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' looks like the adjective meaning ornate, but is the verb meaning to expand on.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate on something is to clarify it by giving more detail.

clue.text: Weapons taken up by defenders

parts.note: plays on the idiom of taking up arms in someone's defence: clubs are the arms seized by those who champion a cause

explanation.surface: Arms seized by those guarding a position.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'take up the cudgels' for someone is a British idiom meaning to defend them vigorously.
explanation.definitionFit: Short thick clubs used as weapons are what champions of a cause proverbially take up.

clue.text: Fixing of competition to prepare for joint share distribution?

definitions.meaning: a rigged arrangement in which rivals share out a market between themselves

definitions.text: to prepare for joint share distribution?
definitions.meaning: read literally, slicing a roast joint into portions to share out

explanation.surface: A rigged contest likened to readying a stake to be shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like joint ownership but is a joint of meat; 'share' is a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest division of spoils among parties is a slicing up, as of meat.

clue.text: Squashes relatively new boy?

definitions.meaning: relatively in the sense of a relative: a son who joins a family by marriage

explanation.surface: A newcomer at school gets crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' means by family relationship: a spouse's son is a new relation.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading on something flattens it, and a husband's or wife's son from an earlier marriage is a new family member.

clue.text: Buzzer not working

definitions.meaning: something that buzzes: a male bee
describes an idler; the noun names a lazy person who lives off others' work

explanation.surface: A doorbell or alarm that has broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a faulty buzzer; really it is a male bee, and the same word names a lazy hanger-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A male honeybee hums and does no work in the hive, which is why the word also names a loafer.

clue.text: Had a row with an inner circle at first

annotationWithheld.why: Had a row with an inner circle at first (5): 'Had a row' defines OARED, but no sound parse of the rest gives the letters; O (circle) first plus A plus RED would need 'inner' to mean RED, which nothing supports.
annotationWithheld.clue: Had a row with an inner circle at first

clue.text: For each drink, note, use filter.

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
cola is a soft drink
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Instructions for making coffee: for every cup, remember to use a filter.
explanation.walkthrough: TE (also spelt ti) is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a liquid slowly through a porous filter is to seep through it, as coffee does.

clue.text: Miner working in gallery is cut off

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters go inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a famous art gallery in London

indicators.note: working means the letters of miner are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A mineworker employed in an art gallery loses his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' is the anagram signal: it looks like the miner's job, but it tells you to rearrange MINER, and the gallery is the TATE in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To end or discontinue something is to cut it off, as with a contract or a call.

clue.text: They expect to succeed in sound broadcasts

indicators.note: in sound means the word for broadcasts is heard rather than spelt, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it, so airs are broadcasts

explanation.surface: People hoping for success in radio programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' looks like achieving success, but means taking over from someone, as an inheritor does.
explanation.definitionFit: Successors in line to inherit a title or estate are waiting for their turn.

clue.text: Continental way in which daughter interrupts is so impolite

indicators.note: interrupts means the abbreviation breaks into the word for street

parts.note: rue is French for street, a way on the Continent

explanation.surface: A French street where a girl keeps cutting in on conversations, which is bad manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-mannered behaviour is discourteous and offensive.

clue.text: Shoot dangerous monster in the plant

parts.note: to snap is to take a photograph, to shoot a picture
a dragon is a fearsome mythical beast

explanation.surface: Kill a fearsome beast lurking among the vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' suggests firing a gun, or a plant's shoot, but it means take a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: Antirrhinum is a garden flower whose blooms open like jaws when squeezed.
